# Trip Log Norway

## Summary
Nine days in Norway at the end of June, split between Bergen and the fjord country inland. I flew into Bergen, spent four nights there, then took the train east to Myrdal and rode the Flam railway down to the village. From Flam I worked my way back along the water by bus and a fjord ferry, which turned out to be the best two hours of the whole trip. The weather was mixed, as everyone warned me: two grey days, one proper downpour, and the rest bright and cool. I walked a lot and did not rent a car, which kept things cheap and simple.

## Highlights
Bergen on the first evening, wandering Bryggen before the crowds arrived. The Flam railway was every bit as good as people say, especially the stretch past the waterfall where the train stops. The fjord ferry gave me walls of rock on both sides and water so still it mirrored the cliffs. I hiked up above Flam one afternoon and watched the cruise ships come in far below. In Bergen I ate far too many cinnamon buns and spent a rainy morning in the fish market. The light at midnight was strange and lovely.

## Costs
Total came to 1450 EUR for the nine days, which is close to what I had budgeted. Flights were 210 EUR return, booked early. The train and the Flam railway together were 180 EUR, and the fjord ferry was 65 EUR. Accommodation ran to 620 EUR, mostly a hostel in Bergen and two nights in a small guesthouse by the water. Food and coffee came to about 300 EUR. The rest went on local buses, a museum ticket and the inevitable souvenir jumper.
